effects.target: will

on_failure.target: 2 temporary negative levels for 1 day per caster level; a prepared caster also loses one prepared spell from her highest level for each negative level, a spontaneous caster loses one highest-level slot and knowledge of one random spell of that level; if the negative levels equal or exceed her character level she falls catatonic instead of dying

mindwipe.notes: Negative levels are not in the condition vocabulary and there is no 'negative level' effect type, so the whole payload is one narrative spec. Printed duration is instantaneous; the negative levels themselves last 1 day/caster level, which is stated in the narrative text rather than in `duration`.

effects.target: Creates one unattended, nonmagical object of nonliving vegetable matter, up to 1 cubic foot per caster level. A complex item needs a successful Craft check. A created object cannot serve as a material component.

minor-creation.notes: Creation conjuration: the vocabulary has no way to say 'an object now exists', so narrative is the floor.

effects.target: Sends a message of up to 20 words into the dreams of a sleeping creature at any distance; the messenger must be you or a gnome you touch. Fails outright if the recipient is awake.

minor-dream.notes: Duration is 'see text' in the corpus, so no duration is emitted rather than guessing one.

effects.target: Creates a visual figment of up to four 10-foot cubes plus one per caster level that also produces minor sounds but no understandable speech; a creature that interacts with it may disbelieve with a Will save.

minor-image.notes: Corpus duration is 'concentration + rounds (2)'. The structured shape cannot hold both terms, so the tail the engine can actually time (2 rounds after concentration ends) is emitted; the concentration prefix is stated here.

effects.target: Creates a semi-real illusory object of nonliving plant matter up to 1 cubic foot per caster level; any creature that interacts with it may attempt a Will save to make it cease to exist. A gnome may substitute Spellcraft for any Craft check the item requires.

minor-phantom-object.notes: The Will save destroys the object rather than affecting a creature, so it is not modelled as a save_gate over a creature effect.

effects.note: immediate action once you are below half your maximum hit points; ends the spell

minor-reversion.notes: The heal is on the caster and is real (1d8 + 1/level, max +5), but it is conditional: you must be at half hit points or more to cast, and can only draw on it once, after dropping below half. No damage_type is claimed — the prose calls it absorbing strength from an Akashic replica, not positive energy.

effects.note: each target may spend an immediate action once she is below half her maximum hit points; ends the spell on her

minor-reversion-mass.notes: As minor reversion but one creature per level and the bonus caps at +25.

effects.target: You request an effect of your deity: duplicate any cleric spell of 8th level or lower, any other spell of 7th level or lower, undo the harmful effects of spells such as feeblemind or insanity, or an effect of comparable power. Duplicated spells use save DCs as a 9th-level spell. A far more powerful request (raising fallen allies mid-battle, error-free planar travel for the party, warding a city from a natural disaster) costs 25,000 gp of powdered diamond. A request out of line with the deity's nature is refused.

miracle.notes: Open-ended wish-class spell; there is nothing to convert without inventing the effect the player asks for. Duration and save are 'see text' in the corpus, so neither is emitted.

effects.target: Makes a stretch of flat land or water appear to hold a simple land formation — a pool, standing stones, a cove, an island. Purely visual: creatures, structures and equipment in the area are unchanged. A creature interacting with it may disbelieve, and one trained in Survival within 120 feet may roll Survival against the save DC instead of a Will save.

mirage.notes: The Survival-for-Will substitution is a rule the save_gate type cannot express (its save field is the three saves only), so it lives in the narrative text.

effects.target: Makes one 20-foot cube per caster level appear to be something else, with audible, visual, tactile and olfactory detail, including adding or altering structures. It cannot disguise, conceal or add creatures. A creature that interacts with it may disbelieve with a Will save.

mirage-arcana.notes: Corpus duration is 'concentration + hours/level (1)'; the per-level tail is emitted and the concentration prefix noted here.

effects.target: Turns a touched mirror into a portal to an extradimensional space holding up to eight Medium creatures. Those inside are hidden from spells and divinations that do not work across planes, can see and hear out as through a window, and may show themselves in the reflection for 1 round at a time. Covering the mirror deactivates the portal; breaking it or moving it more than 5 feet ends the spell and expels everyone inside, leaving them nauseated for 1d6 rounds. Only one creature may enter at a time, and only if it fits through an opening the size of the mirror.

mirror-hideaway.notes: The nauseated 1d6 rounds is NOT emitted as an apply_condition: the spell's target is a mirror, nobody is nauseated on casting, and the condition only lands on the occupants when the mirror is broken or moved. Modelling it as the spell's own effect would sicken whoever the spell was aimed at.

effects.target: Creates 1d4 illusory doubles of you plus one per three caster levels (maximum eight) that share your square and mimic you. Each attack or attack-roll spell aimed at you may hit an image instead — roll randomly among you and the images; a hit on a figment destroys it, and a miss by 5 or less destroys one too. Area effects and effects with no attack roll affect you normally and destroy no images. An attacker who cannot see the images (you invisible, attacker blind) is not fooled.

mirror-image.notes: No `scaling` emitted: the per-level progression is a count of decoy images, not damage or healing dice, and the scaling block only describes dice. VOCABULARY GAP — there is no effect type for a miss chance or a pool of decoys, which is the whole of what this spell does.

effects.target: Polishes up to one square foot of a smooth, contiguous metal item — a breastplate, helm, shield or sword, but not a mace or mail — until it is reflective enough to serve as a mirror. It gains no protection from later damage or corrosion.

Hit both and you deal half damage to each; hit one and you deal it normal damage. On a critical threat you roll one confirmation against both — confirm against both for half critical damage each, confirm against one and it is an ordinary hit.
the split attack roll and its critical confirmation, if the two selected opponents are flanking you

mirror-strike.notes: The +2 is written as situational_mod, not combat_mod, on purpose: it applies only when the two chosen opponents are flanking you, and a combat_mod would have the engine hand out +2 to every attack roll for the duration. The prose's bonus type is unstated, so untyped. Corpus duration is 'see text'; the prose says the spell ends if unused by the end of your next turn, which is until_discharged.

effects.target: As mirror hideaway — the touched mirror becomes a portal to an extradimensional space — except a creature inside may spend a swift action to exit through any other mirror within 500 feet as if using dimension door, one way, provided it fits through an opening that mirror's size. on_failure.target: The creature's shadow is subtly altered — small horns, over-long arms — and a spirit inhabits it. No more than once every 10 minutes, as an immediate action, the shadow interferes with its host or an adjacent creature by manipulating their shadows, and a haunt-like manifestation occurs that round. You direct it while within range; otherwise the GM times it, usually at a crucial roll. Does not work on creatures that cast no shadow or reflection.
one attack roll, combat maneuver check, or Strength- or Dexterity-based skill check, each time the shadow disrupts (no more than once per 10 minutes)

mischievous-shadow.notes: The disruption is either the -8 or the concentration check, chosen per use, so both are written and neither is a standing modifier — situational_mod is narrated, not applied. 'Once every 10 minutes' cannot be said in the `uses` vocabulary (per_day/per_combat/per_hour/once only), so it is stated in the text.

effects.target: One creature or object of up to a 10-foot cube is detected as if it were another object you chose within range at casting — aura, alignment, magic, truthfulness and so on all read as the decoy's. The caster of a detection may attempt a Will save to see through it. Affects only divinations that reveal auras (detect evil, detect magic, discern lies), not augury, detect thoughts or scrying.

misdirection.notes: The Will save belongs to the diviner peering in, not to the spell's target, so it is not a save_gate over the target's effects.

on_failure.target: The creature cannot attack the warded target (as sanctuary — it must attempt the save each time it tries, and if it fails it loses the action) and feels a strong pity toward it, taking it for weak, pathetic and no threat.

effects.target: If the warded target breaks the spell by attacking, every creature that had failed its save gains a +2 morale bonus on attack rolls against the target for 1 minute.

miserable-pity.notes: The +2 morale bonus is deliberately NOT a combat_mod: it goes to the target's enemies, and only after the warded target breaks the spell. Converting it would have handed the spell's own subject a +2 to attack. Corpus duration is 'rounds/level (1) and minutes (1) (see text)'; the per-level term is the ward, and the 1 minute is the backfire window.

effects.target: You turn invisible as greater invisibility for 1 round per caster level regardless of concentration, and an illusory double of you (as major image) appears within range. From the round after casting you direct the double with concentration; it moves at your speed, talks and gestures and can pretend to attack or cast, but cannot do either. It lasts as long as you concentrate plus 3 rounds, then carries on with its last activity until the duration expires. You may superimpose it on yourself at casting so observers see no switch.

mislead.notes: Corpus duration is 'rounds/level (1) and concentration + rounds (3)'. The per-level term (the greater invisibility) is emitted; the double's concentration + 3 rounds is stated in the text.

effects.target: Choose one at casting. Prepare: you prepare up to three additional levels of spells (a cantrip counts as half a level). Retain: a spell of 3rd level or lower that you cast up to 1 round before you began casting returns to your mind. Either way the spells fade after 24 hours if uncast.

mnemonic-enhancer.notes: Acts on the caster's own spell preparation, which the effect vocabulary has no type for.

effects.target: Inscribes a dormant rune on a touched object, which reads as magic aura. While a spellcaster holds it, any spell she casts that is on your spell list has a 10% chance of being absorbed — it fails as if countered, and its knowledge appears in your mind for 24 hours, long enough to prepare it in an unused slot, write it into a spellbook, or teach it to your familiar. The rune absorbs one spell per two caster levels before it is discharged. Knowledge of a spell you could not learn normally is useless to you.

mnemonic-siphon.notes: Corpus duration is 'days/level (1) or until discharged'; the shape holds one kind, so the per-level term is emitted and the discharge condition (one spell per 2 caster levels) is in the text.

effects.target: Each affected ally within the 50-foot burst may, once, double a morale bonus it is already benefiting from on a single roll or check, declared before the roll. Using it discharges the spell for that creature; a creature with no morale bonus gets nothing.

moment-of-greatness.notes: Doubling a bonus that already exists is not a modifier with an amount, so no combat_mod could be written without inventing a number. VOCABULARY GAP — no effect type multiplies an existing bonus.

effects.target: Once during the duration you gain an insight bonus equal to your caster level (maximum +25) on a single attack roll, combat maneuver check, opposed ability or skill check, or saving throw, or to your AC against one attack even while flat-footed. Declaring it takes no action and may happen on another creature's turn, but must come before the roll. Using it ends the spell, and you may only have one active at a time.

moment-of-prescience.notes: Refused to write this as a situational_mod: `amount` is an integer field and the bonus is 'equal to your caster level', so any number put there would be invented. VOCABULARY GAP — only save_gate's `dc` accepts a formula; modifier amounts cannot scale with caster level.

nine-lives.notes: The 3d6 of Rejuvenate is real healing on the target, but it is one option of six drawing on a shared pool of nine uses and only fires at 0 hit points. A heal spec would heal the target 3d6 the moment the ward was cast. Same reasoning for the six remove_condition specs Shake Off could suggest: the target picks one condition, once, when it chooses. Roll 1d6 per 2 caster levels as a dice pool, and spend each die exactly once. Match any number of dice against the Eight Basic Energies table to fix the energy types dealt; allocate one die to the number of creatures affected including the first (no two of them more than 15 feet apart); allocate any number of dice to range, which becomes 10 times their sum in feet. The remaining dice are summed, and that is the damage to the first creature hit — a successful Reflex save halves it. Secondary targets take 50% of that figure rounded up, and a successful Reflex save negates it for them.

numerological-evocation.notes: Refused to emit a damage spec or a `scaling` block. The pool is 1d6 per 2 caster levels, but the player spends an unknown share of it on energy type, target count and range before the leftovers become damage, so neither the dice nor the damage type is knowable in advance. A scaling block of 1d6/2 levels would claim the whole pool as damage, which it never is.

effects.target: Roll 5d8 as a dice pool and spend each die exactly once: one die matched against the Eight Basic Energies table sets which energy is resisted, one sets how many creatures within range are protected including yourself, one sets how many rounds it lasts, and the last two are summed to give the points of resistance granted.

numerological-resistance.notes: No `resistance` spec and no `duration`: the energy type, the amount and the number of rounds are all rolled at casting, so naming any of them would be inventing the roll. Corpus duration is 'see text', which is exactly this.

effects.target: Draws groundwater to the surface in any natural terrain on the Material Plane, creating a permanent spring yielding 5 gallons of pure drinking water per caster level each hour, with a pond if the ground suits. In desert, a DC 25 caster level check is needed to make the spring at all and it yields only 1 gallon per caster level per day, and erosion may block an untended flow before vegetation takes hold. Arctic cold may freeze it; tropical parasites may foul it where the water stands stagnant.

oasis.notes: Printed duration is instantaneous, but the spring it leaves behind is permanent — stated in the text rather than overriding the corpus.

effects.target: Creatures perceive you normally, but when one stops observing you it must succeed at a Will save (spell resistance applies) or lose all memory of having been aware of you and of what you did while the spell lasted. It still notices everything else about itself and its surroundings — a guard remembers running and may spot a door now unlocked, but not that he was chasing you. The listed duration is how long you carry the effect; the memory loss itself is instantaneous and can only be undone by magic such as modify memory.

out-of-sight.notes: The Will save is rolled by observers, not by the caster who is the spell's target, so it is not a save_gate.

The focus book fills with snippets from libraries across the world. You may read for up to 1 round per caster level, to a maximum of 10, and may stop whenever you like. When you stop you immediately attempt one Knowledge check with a +1 circumstance bonus for each round you studied, to a maximum of +10. The writing fades when the spell ends, and if you do not make a Knowledge check on the round you stop reading, you gain nothing.

page-bound-epiphany.notes: The bonus is +1 per round spent reading, decided in play, so no fixed amount can be written into a skill_mod.

If the effect also targeted you or included you in its area, you suffer it twice — once for yourself and once for the creature you spared.

passing-fancy.notes: Deliberately NOT apply_condition fascinated. The prose says the target is 'fascinated by the topic' in plain English, but the 1e fascinated condition means an entranced creature that takes no actions, where this target walks around and talks — applying it would freeze a creature the spell leaves mobile. The -10 falls on onlookers, not the target. No `duration` emitted: the corpus says 'rounds (4d4)' and the duration shape takes an integer amount, so 4d4 rounds cannot be written without picking a number. FORMAT GAP — duration amounts cannot be dice.

When the spell expires, anyone inside the passage is ejected from the nearest exit; if it is dispelled or you dismiss it, they are ejected from the far exit where there is one, or the only exit if there is not.

Four 5-foot squares, one of which must be your own, glow with dim light. From your next turn you may extend the glow by another four squares as a swift action, each new square adjacent to one already glowing. Any ally that ends its turn on a glowing square, including one who falls unconscious there, is healed of 1 point of damage.

path-of-glory.notes: The 1 point is not a heal spec: it is healing that repeats every round, to whichever allies happen to be standing on the lit squares, and a heal spec would heal the caster 1 point once at casting and never again. Same reason the brief gives for repeating damage.

effects.target: As path of glory — four 5-foot squares glow, extendable by four more each turn as a swift action — except an ally that ends its turn on a glowing square is healed of 5 points of damage instead of 1.

path-of-glory-greater.notes: Repeating healing to whoever stands on the squares, as path of glory.

effects.target: A 40-foot-high downdraft equivalent to a windstorm fills a 100-foot line. In the first round it sweeps the area clear of everything Small or smaller, blowing each outward to one side or the other with even odds. You may move within the effect without penalty; every other creature is subject to the wind. From the second round on, the edges of the effect act as a wind wall. Over water or another liquid it carves a channel up to 40 feet deep. On your turn, as a move action, you may rotate it up to 45 degrees about either end or slide it up to 50 feet along its own line, toward you or away.

path-of-the-winds.notes: Corpus duration is 'concentration + rounds (1)'; the 1-round tail is emitted and the concentration prefix noted. The Fortitude save is against the wind's effects on creatures caught in the line, and windstorm's own rules supply what happens, so nothing is claimed here.

effects.target: You notice unusual breaks in patterns — stones in a wall, boards in a floor, cracks in glass, trees in a forest. You gain an insight bonus equal to half your caster level (minimum +1, maximum +10) on Search checks, and the same bonus on Survival checks to follow tracks. It grants neither the Track feat, nor trapfinding, nor any ability to disable traps, but works alongside them if you have them.

pattern-recognition.notes: The bonus is half caster level, a formula no modifier `amount` can hold. The prose says 'Search checks', a 3.5 skill Pathfinder folded into Perception; the wording is left as printed rather than silently retargeted to a skill the spell never names.
